summary: Collects high-level requirements for tightly coupled SIP conferences, the kind where a central party manages the call. It examines a wide range of needs. Later documents are meant to map these onto existing protocol pieces and to define new extensions, together forming a guide for interoperable SIP conferencing applications.

eli5.summary: Before building a group phone call system, you list everything it should do. This memo is that list, so the later building plans can be checked against it.

questions: what is a sip conference focus
what is tightly coupled sip conferencing
what are the requirements for sip conferencing
subtitle: The checklist of what a central-server SIP conference has to be able to do.

tldr.problem: SIP handles calls between two parties well, but building interoperable multiparty conferences needs agreed requirements for creating, joining, managing and ending them.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines a tightly coupled conference as a star around a central focus and lists numbered requirements (REQ-n) for discovery, creation, termination, participant handling, conference state, focus migration, side-bars, cascading and SIMPLE coordination.
tldr.outcome: It only lists requirements. Separate documents are to map them onto existing protocol pieces and define extensions.

facts.label: Conference topology
facts.value: Always a star around the focus

facts.label: Dialogs per participant
facts.value: One SIP dialog with the focus

today: RFC 4245 is an Informational memo with no recorded obsoleting or updating RFC. It records requirements only and defines no protocol itself.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 4245 collects a wide range of requirements for tightly coupled conferencing based on SIP (RFC 3261). The requirements are grouped by subject so solutions can progress in parallel. Separate documents are to map them to existing protocol primitives, define new protocol extensions and introduce new protocols where needed. Together they are meant to be a guide for interoperable SIP conferencing applications.

Requirement keywords MAY, SHOULD and MUST follow RFC 2119. Requirements for conferencing policy, media mixing, floor control and privilege control are left to separate documents.
sections.eli5: This is a to-do list for people building group calls, not the instructions for building them.

sections.title: The Tightly Coupled Model
sections.content:
A SIP conference is an association of SIP user agents (the participants) with a central point, the conference focus. The focus keeps a separate SIP dialog with each participant, so the conference graph is always a star, and the focus links the dialogs together internally.

The focus can be run by a participant, which typically hosts only a simple ad hoc conference using basic SIP call control. Or it can be a dedicated conference server, which adds simultaneous, large scalable, reserved and managed conferences. A server may support any subset of the advanced functions.

Media can be centralized (sessions between the focus and each participant), decentralized (a multicast or multi-unicast mesh among participants), or a mix that may differ per media type. Conference policies are the parameters and rules set at the start, such as maximum participants, chair supervision, password protection, duration or the way of media mixing. Conference state is the information about the conference in progress, such as participants, media sessions, the loudest speaker and the chair.
sections.eli5: A group call is like a hub with spokes: everybody talks to the person in the middle, who connects everyone together.

sections.title: Creating, Joining and Ending Conferences
sections.content:
Discovery requirements include finding conferencing servers, checking whether a SIP address-of-record has focus abilities, and locating a conference focus, its properties and its state from a global conference identifier. The memo says standard means for these functions by automata MUST be defined.

For creation, a means MUST exist to create ad hoc or reserved conference identifiers, with properties set by default, by profile or explicitly. For termination, a user agent MUST be able to disconnect everyone and release resources, and a means MAY be defined to revert a two-party conference to a basic point-to-point SIP session.

Participant handling covers conference-unaware user agents (a plain RFC 3261 user agent MUST be able to dial in and be invited), dial-out and dial-in scenarios that each use a single SIP dialog, third-party invitation (with "mass invitation" as a SHOULD), and removal of participants (with "mass ejection" as a MAY). Invitations MUST carry a standard indication that it is a conference, plus the identifier.

Privacy requirements say a focus SHOULD support joining anonymously (presence announced, identity not disclosed) and in hidden mode (neither presence nor identity disclosed). Participants MAY support them.
sections.eli5: The list covers how to find a meeting, start one, invite or remove people, join with an ordinary phone, and listen in without people knowing who you are.

sections.title: State, Focus Migration and Side-bars
sections.content:
Conference state is treated as a virtual database. It MUST be modular so aspects can be read independently, reports MUST be able to combine aspects, and an extensible registration mechanism MUST exist. A default report SHOULD list at least the current participants. Changes MUST be reportable in a timely manner to interested parties, including non-participants. A user agent must be able to ask for selected changes only, set a minimum interval between reports, and have recent changes aggregated. State must also be available on demand.

For focus role migration, procedures MUST be defined to delegate the role, to request a transfer, to transfer it unconditionally, and to detect a focus failure.

Side-bar requirements cover joining, being invited to, and creating side-bar conferences inside the main one, including by conference-unaware user agents and without extra SIP dialogs with the focus; some of those MAY use non-SIP means.

The memo notes that "cascading of conferences" has several meanings, such as peer-to-peer signaling chains, hierarchical signaling, or distributed media mixing only, and each implies different requirements. It also asks that SIMPLE presence and instant messaging fit the SIP conferencing architecture and that combined multimedia and IM conferences and side-bars be addressed.
sections.eli5: Everyone should be able to see who is in the call, someone else should be able to take over as host if needed, and small private chats can happen inside the big one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Every operation described needs to be authorized by a focus or a participant, expected to follow authorization rules in the conference policy. To enforce policy, the focus must be able to authenticate potential participants, and the memo says normal SIP mechanisms such as Digest authentication and certificates can be used. Details are left to the protocol documents.

Conferencing also has privacy implications. Standard SIP mechanisms for requesting privacy should be used by a focus and will be detailed in the protocol documents.
sections.eli5: Only people who are allowed should be able to do things in the call, so the host must check who is who.
